Where it began

Imam-ul-Haq was born in December 1995 in Pakistan's Punjab. Cricket runs in the family: his uncle is Inzamam-ul-Haq, the former Pakistan captain.

He made his name at home, in the domestic game, and the runs came in big helpings. Batting for Habib Bank Limited in the 2016–17 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy final, he made 200 not out, and a year later he was player of the match in the National T20 Cup final for Lahore Blues.

The player

His international career began in October 2017 with a one-day game against Sri Lanka, and he marked it with a hundred and the match award. Only Saleem Elahi had done that for Pakistan before him. His Test debut followed against Ireland on 11 May 2018, and his fifty in the final innings helped Pakistan to victory.

In March 2022, against Australia, he made his first Test hundred and then a second in the same match, the tenth Pakistan batter to manage a hundred in each innings. By November 2026 he had played 31 Tests, from 2018 to 2026, scoring 1,865 runs at 34.54 with three hundreds, 11 fifties and a best of 157.

What made him special

Imam likes to build an innings brick by brick, and in one-day cricket that brought runs by the heap. In July 2018 he and Fakhar Zaman put on 304 for the first wicket against Zimbabwe, the biggest opening stand one-day cricket had seen, and he reached 1,000 one-day runs in only 19 innings. By July 2021 he had passed 2,000.

Test cricket asked for a different sort of patience, and his first Test hundred took nearly four years to arrive. When it finally came, against Australia, it brought a friend along in the second innings. His 23 catches show a safe pair of hands as well as a sound defence.

Away from the middle

Imam has enjoyed his visits to England. Somerset signed him for four County Championship matches in 2022, and in 2025 he joined Yorkshire as an overseas player. In that summer's One Day Cup he made 583 runs in seven group innings with three hundreds, among them 159 against Northamptonshire and 117 in a winning chase against Lancashire.

Back home in September 2025 he made 330 for Multan Region in the Hanif Mohammad Trophy, the highest score of his career, with 34 fours and eight sixes. By 2026 he was back in Pakistan's Test side.

And finally

That 330 came from 291 balls at the National Bank Stadium in Karachi. For a man known for his patience, it was remarkably brisk work. The bowlers that week may have wished he had stuck to his careful side.
